meta.hardware: i5 4 cores shared with 3 other agents; numba 1 thread; each script <= 10 min

question: Valerio: 'our lattice must potentially hold the whole Milky Way or the known universe; to see a radio wave whole you zoom far out, but we want to see it'. Build a SPARSE HIERARCHICAL lattice (levels h_k = 2^k h0, only blocks where something is non-zero), the same zig-zag light rule on every level, levels joined by a restriction/prolongation band (as ZOOM_NODO).

design_frozen.rule: massless spin-1 zig-zag walker (F = E + icB), identical on every level (it has no length scale)
design_frozen.time: Berger-Oliger: one level-k tick = two level-(k-1) ticks; each level keeps its own parity
design_frozen.restriction: coarse cell <- 4th-order midpoint interpolation (-1,9,9,-1)/16 per axis, only from fine INTERIOR
design_frozen.prolongation: fine band (outer W=4 fine cells) <- tensor-cubic Lagrange of the coarse level at every sync; band evolves with the fine rule between syncs (no time interpolation)
design_frozen.energy: composite: fine interior + coarse cells not made only of fine-interior children (each point once)
design_frozen.regrid: level k block kept if max|F_k - P(F_k+1)| > tol (coarsest: max|F| > tol), dilated by 1 block, plus parents of the finer level's blocks dilated by 1 block; new blocks by prolongation
design_frozen.free_parameters: B, W=4, interpolation orders (cubic/cubic), tol, halo = engineering choices; 0 physics parameters (c and the rule are those of docs/ZIGZAG.md)

R2a_speed.test: packet lambda = 24 cells, sigma = 4 lambda, on one sparse level with regrid, levels k = 0,1,5,10,20; centroid velocity over 480 own ticks, in physical units (cells*h_k)/(ticks*dt_k)

prediction.axis: PASS on every level (axis shift is exact); arrays bitwise identical across levels
prediction.diagonal_45deg_24cells: FAIL: plane-wave group velocity of the rule -0.87 % (needs >= 32 cells/lambda: -0.48 %)

R2a_speed.also: centroid velocity measured on each side of a level interface in R2b (axis): |v-1| <= 0.5 %

R2b_interface.test: 2-D strip periodic in y; fine level 0 next to coarse level 1; Gaussian packet sigma = 3 lambda (axis) of helicity +1 crossing fine->coarse and coarse->fine; N = coarse cells per lambda in {2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32}; normal incidence and 30 deg; T = energy beyond the interface (+16 fine cells), R = energy behind it, lost = 1 - T - R (composite energy)
R2b_interface.criterion: for N >= 16: T >= 99 %, R <= 1 %, both directions, normal incidence (headline); 30 deg reported with the same thresholds
R2b_interface.prediction: PASS at N >= 16 with R < 1e-4 (cubic interpolation error ~ (k h_c)^4); short waves N <= 4 MUST fail (T < 90 %): a coarse lattice cannot carry them, physics of every multigrid; reported as a curve

R2c_phase_helicity.test: transmitted packet compared on the coarse grid with the same packet evolved on the uniform lattice of its origin level (no interface); helicity fractions from the lattice eigen-projectors of the two-tick walk
R2c_phase_helicity.criterion: normal incidence, N >= 16: |phase error| <= 0.01 rad, fidelity |<ref|out>|/(|ref||out|) >= 0.999, wrong helicity + static mode <= 1e-3 of the transmitted energy; 30 deg: fidelity and helicity only (the phase there also contains the different dispersion of the two levels)

R2_3D.test: same as R2b in 3-D (blocks 8^3, strip periodic in y and z), N = 16 and 8, normal incidence

R3_demo.world: ONE world, levels 0..20: gamma pulse lambda = 24 h0 at level 0 (sigma = 18 h0, moving +x), radio pulse lambda = 24 h20 = 24*2^20 h0 at level 20 (sigma = 36 h20, moving at 60 deg), the gamma inside the radio envelope; levels 1..19 exist only as a nested 'chimney' around the gamma

criteria.cells: total active cells <= 1e6 and field memory <= 100 MB at all times
criteria.radio: after n_r >= 1 level-20 ticks (target 2): radio on level 20 vs the same radio evolved alone: relative L2 difference <= 1e-3
criteria.gamma: after 2^20 n_r level-0 ticks: centroid moved 2^20 n_r h0 +- 0.5 h0, fidelity vs the exactly shifted initial packet >= 0.999, energy conserved within 1e-3

R3_demo.prediction: PASS; wall time in Python+numba ~10-20 min per radio tick (2^20 gamma ticks): TIME, not memory, is the wall
R3_demo.figure: lab/out/reticolo_zoom_*.png, zoom-out ladder from level 0 to level 20

R4_scaling.claim: active cells to hold a pulse of wavelength lambda in a box L = (cells at its home level, independent of the absolute scale) + (number of levels) x (chimney blocks)
R4_scaling.test: same packet at home level k = 0..40 (cells must be identical), plus worlds with two pulses 2^m apart in wavelength, m = 0..40 (overhead must grow linearly with m)
